title: “Trust but not blind trust”: accounting controls and level-specific budget decoupling in a public-sector organization
journal: Journal of Public Budgeting, Accounting & Financial Management
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how a beyond budgeting (BB)-inspired reconfiguration of accounting controls supports trust-based management practices in a public-sector organization operating under annual budget constraints. While BB advocates replacing traditional annual budgeting with more adaptive and trust-based approaches, public organizations face strong accountability demands that make the abandonment of annual budgets difficult. Design/methodology/approach This study is based on a longitudinal, exploratory case study of the National Service and Call Center at Norway’s Labour and Welfare Administration. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with managers and employees, as well as an analysis of internal documents, reports and governmental directives. Findings The study shows how annual budgeting was decoupled across organizational levels. While annual budgets were retained for political and departmental accountability, budget-based resource pre-allocation was abandoned at the operational level. Instead, the organization developed oversight controls – periodic, transparent and comparative accounting practices such as cost monitoring, forecasting and internal benchmarking. These controls supported decentralized decision-making, while preserving financial discipline based on values-based decision-making. The findings further show that increased autonomy fostered trust but also generated employee anxiety, which was mitigated through intensified leadership practices supported by oversight control mechanisms. Originality/value The study contributes to the trust–control literature by demonstrating how accounting controls can complement trust-based management, and to BB research by showing how BB principles can be adapted to public-sector contexts.

title: “The place alphabet” as a method for analyzing architectural context. Drawing as a tool for understanding
journal: Journal of Civil Engineering, Environment and Architecture
abstract: This article presents the Place Alphabet method as a tool for the analysis of architectural context based on field observations and freehand drawing. The point of departure for the described method is the concept of the Kazimierz Alphabet, developed by Konrad Kucza–Kuczyński. This concept has been further developed and formulated as a systematic research procedure applicable in any cultural and geographical context. The article discusses the role of architectural drawing as a cognitive medium and a tool of synthesis. It presents the Kazimierz Alphabet as the foundation of the method and describes the successive stages of the Place Alphabet method, including field observations, drawing documentation, analysis of recurring motifs, identification of the letters of the alphabet, and the formulation of the alphabet itself. The effectiveness of the method was verified through field research conducted in Bahrain. During this research, the author created 60 field drawings documenting the characteristic features of the local cultural landscape. The proposed method enables the synthetic identification of the characteristic elements constituting the identity of a place and their representation in the form of drawings. The findings indicate that the Place Alphabet method may serve as a universal tool for the analysis of architectural context, making it possible not only to define the existing relationships and characteristics of a place but also to formulate design assumptions based on an in-depth understanding of its identity.

title: When AI service appearance backfires: form-based expectations and trust fragility
abstract: Purpose This research aims to explore why high-fidelity digital human avatars induce a stronger adverse response from customers than an artificial static robot interface condition following a service failure. Design/methodology/approach A total of three studies were performed. Studies 1 and 2 (n = 322, n = 282) involved a between-subjects design that was set up in the context of educational administration and aimed at investigating the effects of the main variable, the mediation mechanism and the moderation effects of the size of the failure. Study 3 (n = 205), on the other hand, adopted a post-performance only design involving adults in the banking sector. Findings The findings suggest that service failure by a high-fidelity digital human avatar creates a much larger drop in trust than a similar failure by a static chatbot. This effect is partially mediated by a higher experience of expectancy violation, and this effect is amplified in the case of a more serious service failure. The results were replicated in the retail banking context, and the indirect effect of perceived expectation violation was still significant while holding discomfort, perceived deception and institutional blame constant. Originality/value This research questions the dominant notion of the more human, the better in AI service design by examining the unique susceptibility of customer trust. This research recognizes service failure as an important boundary condition to the normally positive effect of designing a high fidelity digital human avatar. This research proves that if there is failure on the part of the high fidelity digital human avatar, then the higher expectations created by the avatar may create an erosion of trust.

title: What does it take to bring employees back to office? Driving reattachment and engagement through compassionate team and dependable supervisors
abstract: Purpose In this study, we investigate the impact of pandemic-induced disruptions and subsequent changes in work arrangements on employee's responses to return to a work-from-office environment. Our premise is two-fold – first, we examine reattachment and engagement levels of the employees with their return to the work-from-office environment and their impact on individual performance and work withdrawal behaviours. Second, we explore the moderating roles of supervisory dependence and perceived team compassionate behaviour in the above relationships. Design/methodology/approach We utilised a two-phase panel design drawing on data from 250 employees in the Indian IT sector, capturing employee responses immediately following their return to the work-from-office environment and again six months later. Findings Results revealed that the non-significant impact of job reattachment on performance changed to a positive significant impact, while the impact of work withdrawal reduced over a six-month duration. Job engagement was found to be a significant mediator in the reattachment–performance and reattachment–withdrawal links. Further, supervisory dependence was found to be a significant moderator in the reattachment–engagement link, and it demonstrated a significant moderated-mediation effect in phase 1 but became non-significant in phase 2. Perceived team compassionate behaviour remained a significant moderator in both phases and demonstrated a significant moderated-mediation effect, highlighting the enduring role of peer-level support during return-to-work-from-office transitions. Originality/value This unique study offers insights into how employees psychologically reattach to work during transitions back to office-based environments following prolonged work-from-home or hybrid arrangements.

title: Utilization of a Contextualized English Reading Module to Enhance Higher-Order Thinking Skills among Grade 10 Students through Socially Relevant Topics
journal: International Journal of Transformative Multidisciplinary Studies
abstract: Philippine secondary education faces challenges in English literacy and higher-order thinking skills (HOTS), as evidenced by low PISA scores and declining EPI rankings. Philippine reading intervention strategies are based on lower-order fluency rather than on critical and analytical thinking. This study developed and tested a Contextualized English Reading Enhancement Module to improve the HOTS of Grade 10 learners through socially relevant issues. It employed a pre-experimental, single-group mixed-methods design at Fortune High School in Marikina City for the year 2025-2026. Forty-two Grade 10 pupils were tested. In order to determine the module structure consisting of 5 lessons, 10 local English teachers and 42 students were surveyed to find 5 relevant social topics: overcoming problems, family relationships, technology and social media, academic pressures, and culture; and 5 least demonstrated HOTS: problem-solving, evaluating, analytical thinking, critical thinking, and metacognition. The data for pretest-posttest comparisons using the Phil-IRI BOSY and MOSY were used to determine the effectiveness of the instruction. Ten teachers reviewed the module. The paired-samples t-test revealed a significantly higher posttest score (M = 21.67) than the pretest score (M = 15.60), t(41) = 8.04, p < .001. The Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test showed that the Phil-IRI significantly improved (W = 331.0, p = 0.034). Overall weighted mean = 3.54; teacher-evaluators have strongly agreed on the quality of the module. The contextualized reading module, based on students’ lived social experiences and Bloom’s revised taxonomy, could help enhance HOTS performance among Grade 10 Filipino students in a single-school setting.

title: The topology of a family tree graph and its members’ satisfaction with one another: a machine learning approach
abstract: Background Family members’ satisfaction with one another is an important component of family well-being, yet most quantitative studies examine specific dyadic or household-level variables rather than the overall topology of the family tree. Methods We present an exploratory machine-learning framework for studying whether family-tree topology contains predictive information about reported family satisfaction. In the proposed approach, each family is represented as a topology-only graph whose nodes correspond to family members and whose edges encode family relationships. A Variational Graph AutoEncoder (VGAE) is used to obtain latent graph representations, which are then used in supervised regression models to predict Extended Family Satisfaction (EFS) and Nuclear Family Satisfaction (NFS). The approach is evaluated on a self-selected online convenience sample of N = 486 families recruited through social-media platforms, using a family-level train/test protocol. Results The proposed topology-based representation showed predictive performance for reported family satisfaction and was compared with regression models based on established aggregate family variables and additional graph-based baselines. These results suggest that family-tree topology may contain information relevant to reported satisfaction, although the evidence remains predictive and exploratory. Conclusion The findings provide preliminary evidence that graph-based representations of family structure can support the study of family satisfaction. However, the results should not be interpreted as causal or population-level conclusions, given the study’s sampling limitations, low response rate, and absence of sociodemographic control variables.

title: The relationship between latent profiles of parental rejection and Chinese adolescents’ test anxiety: the mediating role of sense of security
The Björck classification of the open abdomen revisited: clarifying concepts for modern complex abdomen management
abstract: Abstract Introduction The open abdomen (OA) has become an integral component of modern acute care, trauma, and vascular surgery. Since 2009, the Björck classification, amended in 2016, has provided a common language for describing the status and progression of the OA and remains the most widely used system worldwide. More than fifteen years of international experience, together with advances in temporary abdominal closure, negative pressure wound therapy, mesh-mediated fascial traction, critical care, more timely effective septic source control and abdominal wall reconstruction, have broadened the spectrum of patients encountered and altered the natural history of the OA. In this setting, certain concepts within the classification—particularly developing fixation and the frozen abdomen—are interpreted inconsistently among surgeons and institutions. Materials and methods In this narrative review, we revisit the contemporary application of the Björck classification and argue that its principal current challenge is one of interpretive consistency rather than validity. Conclusion We distinguish OA from complex abdomen, clarify the practical meaning of each grade, and emphasise that anatomical grade describes a current state rather than an inevitable trajectory. The aim is to preserve the simplicity and structure of the original framework while improving communication, research comparability, and clinical decision-making in the management of patients with complex OA conditions. To this end we propose that interpretation is enhanced by considering two complementary domains: a contamination domain, already embedded in the amended system, and a surgical accessibility domain that describes the progressive loss of operative access from free access through developing fixation to loss of lateral access (the frozen abdomen).
